key_takeaway: trade[XYZ] is currently best modeled as a Privy-enabled retail interface over Hyperliquid / HIP-3, not as a separate low-level trading API stack.

findings: Users can create a new wallet directly in the interface via Privy or connect an existing wallet.
The Privy email wallet path is described as the fastest option for new users without a crypto wallet.
Existing-wallet users must verify wallet control, ensure they are on the Hyperliquid network, deposit funds, and may also need to click Enable Trading and sign another confirmation.
The docs explicitly say users interact with all trade[XYZ] markets using the Hyperliquid API.
The mainnet endpoint is https://api.hyperliquid.xyz and the testnet endpoint is https://api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz.
For XYZ markets, the docs say users should pass type:perpDexs and instruments such as xyz:XYZ100.
All markets accessed through trade[XYZ] operate on Hyperliquid.
The XYZ protocol is described as a HIP-3 DEX instance.
trade[XYZ] is described as the interface and explicitly not the exclusive means of accessing XYZ markets.
The FAQ says Hyperliquid provides the logic for much of the XYZ HIP-3 DEX while trade[XYZ] is the interface.
The FAQ also says Equities [XYZ] markets are distinct from Hyperliquid perp and spot markets, and balances between perp accounts are not shared.
The docs describe trade[XYZ] as a non-custodial interface for markets on HyperCore / the Hyperliquid blockchain.
The current introduction page says the interface may be unavailable in the U.S. and other restricted jurisdictions.

signals: CSP connect-src includes https://*.hyperliquid.xyz and https://*.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz
CSP connect-src includes wss://*.hyperliquid.xyz and wss://*.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz
HTML contains preconnect and dns-prefetch hints for https://api-ui.hyperliquid.xyz

interpretation: The current docs and the live runtime surface point to the same model: trade[XYZ] is an onboarding and interface layer wrapped around Hyperliquid-native execution.
This means trade[XYZ] should not be modeled as an independent exchange-native private API stack in the same way as venues that issue their own API keys and signatures.
The main retail advantage is smoother onboarding through Privy email wallets.
The main constraints are still Hyperliquid-side activation and deposit flow for connected wallets, separate balance buckets across some market types, and interface-level geographic restrictions.

assessment.key_friction: Privy smooths the front door, but connected-wallet users still face deposit and possible Enable Trading steps, while market/balance separation and jurisdiction restrictions remain real constraints.
